Let the cycle vertices be ordered as \(0,\ldots,12\), and write a zero-sum vector as
\[
c_\ast=-\sum_{i=0}^{12}x_i .
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{z,w}c_zc_w d_s(z,w)^p=x^T M(s,p)x,
\]
where
\[
M_{ij}(s,p)=d_s(i,j)^p-d_s(\ast,i)^p-d_s(\ast,j)^p .
\]

Near \(s=0\), the cycle-to-cycle distances remain the ordinary 13-cycle distances
\[
d_s(i,j)=4\min(|i-j|,13-|i-j|),
\]
and only the \(\ast\)-distances vary. At \(s=0,p=1\), the null vector is
\[
a=(2,-2,1,0,0,2,-2,-2,0,2,0,0,1,-2).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
x_0=(-2,1,0,0,2,-2,-2,0,2,0,0,1,-2).
\]

The conditional matrix \(M(0,1)\) is negative semidefinite with one-dimensional kernel spanned by \(x_0\). A direct LDL certificate is obtained by deleting coordinate \(0\) from \(-M(0,1)\); the pivots are
\[
14,\frac{48}{7},8,8,5,8,8,6,\frac{14}{5},\frac{18}{7},\frac{208}{81},1,
\]
all positive. Since \(x_{0,0}\ne0\), this proves the claimed kernel and negative semidefiniteness.

For \(p>1\),
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dp}\right|_{p=1}\sum_{z,w}a_za_wd_0(z,w)^p=4\tau>0,
\]
so \(p=1\) is the endpoint at \(s=0\). Hence
\[
\wp(0)=1.
\]

Grouping the ordered pairs by their distance gives
\[
\tau=
20\log 2+219\log 3-35\log 5-7\log 7-22\log 11-26\log 13-34\log 17+46\log 23.
\]

It remains to compute the cubic variation of the endpoint. Write
\[
d_s(\ast,i)=r_i+s u_i+s^2v_i,
\]
with
\[
u=(0,0,-1,-1,-1,0,0,0,1,1,1,0,0).
\]
Expanding the kernel equation
\[
M(s,\wp(s))x(s)=0
\]
with
\[
\wp(s)=1+ks^3+O(s^4),\qquad x(s)=x_0+sx_1+s^2x_2+O(s^3),
\]
gives
\[
x_1=\left(0,\frac12,0,0,-\frac12,0,0,0,\frac12,0,0,-\frac12,0\right),
\]
\[
x_2=\left(0,-\frac1{12},0,0,\frac1{12},0,0,0,-\frac1{12},0,0,\frac1{12},0\right).
\]
The order \(s^3\) solvability condition is
\[
x_0^T(M_1x_2+M_2x_1)+k\,x_0^TM_p x_0=0.
\]
Here
\[
x_0^T(M_1x_2+M_2x_1)=-\frac23,
\qquad
x_0^TM_p x_0=4\tau.
\]
Thus
\[
k=\frac{1}{6\tau},
\qquad
\wp'''(0)=6k=\frac1{\tau}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\eta=\tau\,\wp'''(0)=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(1,\;20\log 2+219\log 3-35\log 5-7\log 7-22\log 11-26\log 13-34\log 17+46\log 23,\;1\right)}
\]
